texts.li: {A_nameDef} has come to the council about {B_nameDef}. When {B_nameDef} was chosen as {OFFICE}, {B_pronoun} promised {PROMISE}. That was some weeks ago, and {EVIDENCE}.\n\n{A_nameDef} isn't asking for a new vote. {A_nameDef} is asking what the council means to do about it before the next one.

[stood] {A_nameDef} stood against {B_nameDef} for the seat of {OFFICE}, lost, and has been keeping count ever since. At the election {B_nameDef} promised {PROMISE}. It is halfway to the next vote, and {EVIDENCE}.\n\n{A_nameDef} has brought it to the council, and would like to know whether anyone else has noticed.

[hands:watch] {A_nameDef} came to the council with a face like stone. {B_nameDef} promised {PROMISE} when {B_pronoun} took the seat of {OFFICE}, and {EVIDENCE}. {A_nameDef} would like to hear how those two things fit together, and would like to hear it soon.

[hands:food] The meal sacks are thin and the shelves are thinner, and {A_nameDef} remembers who promised otherwise. When {B_nameDef} was chosen as {OFFICE}, {B_pronoun} promised {PROMISE}. Now {EVIDENCE}, and it is a long way yet to the next vote.

[hands:sick] {A_nameDef} has looked in on the sick and come back angry. {B_nameDef} promised {PROMISE} when {B_pronoun} was chosen as {OFFICE}, and {EVIDENCE}. {A_nameDef} wants the council to say something before the next vote does.

[hands:herd] {A_nameDef} counted the herd this morning, and then counted it again. {B_nameDef} promised {PROMISE} as {OFFICE}, and {EVIDENCE}. {A_nameDef} would like the council to ask {B_objective} about it.

[hands:evening] Nobody has laughed at supper in days, and {A_nameDef} knows whose work that was meant to be. {B_nameDef} promised {PROMISE} as {OFFICE}, and {EVIDENCE}. {A_nameDef} has asked the council whether anyone means to do anything about it.

li.label: Give {B_nameDef} a hand with it
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} gave {B_nameDef} a hand with the work of the seat, and {B_nameDef} was glad of it.

outcomes.li: [hands:watch] {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} walked the walls together from dark until past midnight, from one look-out to the next. Neither of them said much, and {A_nameDef} came back with less to say against {B_objective}.

[hands:food] {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} spent the afternoon bringing in what could be eaten and carrying it to the stores. The shelves are only as much fuller as one afternoon makes them, but {B_nameDef} had help, and said so.
[hands:sick] {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} spent the afternoon scrubbing and carrying, and the colony is cleaner for it. Whether that keeps the promise is for the vote to say.
[hands:herd] {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} spent the afternoon with the animals, bringing them home and seeing to them. {B_nameDef} was glad of the help, and said so.
[hands:evening] {B_nameDef} called everyone together for an evening, and {A_nameDef} came and stayed to the end. Somebody laughed at supper again.

li.label: {B_nameDef} answers for it at supper
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} stood at the end of the supper table and answered for what {B_pronoun} had promised, without excuses. {A_nameDef} listened to all of it, and asked one hard question at the end.

outcomes.li: [stood] {B_nameDef} answered at supper for what {B_pronoun} had promised, with {A_nameDef}, who had stood against {B_objective} for the seat, sitting across the table. It was a long supper. Nobody threw anything.

li.label: Leave it to the vote
li.outcome: The council said a promise made at an election is for the next election to judge. {A_nameDef} said that was a long way off, and went back to work.
